title: Two Pins and a String: The Ellipse Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
Push two pins into a board, loop a string around them, pull it tight with a pencil and go all the way round: you get a perfect oval. The pencil keeps changing its distance from each pin, so why is the curve so neat? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 10, Conic Sections) we find the rule of the ellipse.

You will watch a live pencil run round while its two distances to the foci change and their sum stays fixed at 10. We name the centre, the major and minor axes and the foci, prove a² = b² + c² from one right triangle, derive x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 step by step, and grow the eccentricity e = c/a live to see the ellipse flatten. A pause-and-think question on which axis is major, a worked example with 4x² + 9y² = 36, the exam trap that mixes up c² = a² - b², an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.
